source: All-In Podcast — GPT-5 underwhelms, AI TAM/ROIC/energy, China's advantage, tariffs, Nvidia chip smuggling, Apple buybacks and AI strategy
summary: AI demand for energy is a larger and more durable structural driver than the Inflation Reduction Act, creating a massive new demand signal for power infrastructure.
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI's energy demand represents a structural shift larger and more durable than the Inflation Reduction Act, citing Anthropic's projection of 50 gigawatts of new US power demand over three years — roughly equivalent to the entire annual new US generation capacity. He emphasizes that this demand is uniquely favorable: it is location-specific (tied to datacenter clusters), continuous (24/7 baseload), price-insensitive (hyperscalers will pay premium rates), and skewed toward carbon-free sources, creating an unprecedented demand profile for power infrastructure. Baker frames this as a multi-year structural tailwind for power generation, transmission, and clean energy assets. The investment implication is a long-term bullish view on power infrastructure broadly, with particular relevance to nuclear, natural gas, and grid infrastructure companies that can serve large, reliable, carbon-conscious loads.
detail: Baker states the energy implications of AI are 'probably bigger than the Inflation Reduction Act and certainly will be longer-lasting.' He notes Anthropic's paper calling for 50 gigawatts of US power over three years — roughly equal to all new US capacity added in a year.
